_doc: Block ids are assigned in order starting at 1 (0 is air).
After adding blocks, rerun tools/terraria_dust.py (or extract_assets.sh) so they get Terraria's dust (assets/terraria/tile_dust.json); the test world test checks.
tex: per-face crops (all/top/side/bottom). A crop is {sheet, frames: [[x,y],...], tile: [w,h], tiles: [tw,th], stride}.
Sprite blocks are drawn at their real Terraria size: 32 sprite pixels (2 tiles) per block; pixels_per_block overrides it (tree trunks: 16, one tile per block, like the canopies).

wall: hangs on the side of a block, leaning out (wall_torch: placed when a torch is put on a wall). hidden: not listed in the picker or the test world gallery. settings: draw with that block's placeable method and settings.

wall_variant: placed on the side of a block it becomes that block instead (torch -> wall_torch). wall_tilt (degrees), wall_inset, wall_raise: how a wall block hangs (default: a torch's lean). slippery: you slide on it (ice). side_view: the sprite shows the block from the side, its wall on the left (Terraria's wall torch frames): the model points out of the wall without tilting, and a hull gets its depth from the sprite's thickness. hangs: needs the block above (lanterns). default_method: placeable method before any is picked. transform: the model's default transform before picker changes ({offset: [x, y, z] art pixels, rotation, scale}; a platform's plank is lifted to the top of its block).

biome: counts toward that biome around the player (corruption, crimson). on_break orb: rolls the 'loot' table and counts toward the orb messages. unbreakable: can't be mined (the message says why). station_as: counts as that crafting station. trunk: felling it fells the tree above.
fixed_method: a sprite block that keeps its render (not in the placeable picker).

fall_safe: landing on it causes no fall damage (clouds, like Terraria's). sticky: slows you right down inside it (cobwebs). honey_sticky: touching its side you slide down it slowly and can't move fast across it (Terraria's honey block, Player.StickyMovement); you can still jump off. hot: touching it sets you on fire (Hellstone), unless you are immune to fire blocks. house: what it gives a room for Terraria's housing check (light, chair, table). floats: stays put when the block under it goes. interact bed: right-click sets (or clears) your spawn point; clock: tells the time; sign: right-click to write on it (aim at it to read it).

platform: holds you up from above only (Terraria's platforms): you land on its top, jump up through it and walk under it; Drop down falls through. It needs a block or another platform beside it when placed, and holds up what stands on it.

door: a closed door, naming its open twin (door_closed names the closed one); door_top: the door's upper half. The art is Terraria's open door (Tiles_11, seen face on), frame 0 hinged on the left and frame 1 on the right (scripts/world/doors.gd).
New blocks go at the end: saved worlds store block ids by position in this list.

painting: one of Terraria's paintings (tiles 240-246; trophies and racks too): a wall block whose art is bigger than its cell, centred on it; it needs a solid block behind every cell the art covers and those cells empty, and comes down when a block behind it goes (scripts/world/paintings.gd).

Each frame is one random variant. A frame can also be a list of [x, y] tiles, stacked top to bottom (a cattail cell: its head over a stem). Multi-tile sprites are stitched from tiles on an 18px stride, skipping Terraria's 2px padding.
Cube faces are a mosaic of per_face x per_face tiles (default 2); lower: a different crop for the mosaic's bottom row.
fill_top: on a side face, its grass (pixels nearer the top's colours than the lower crop's soil) takes the top face's texture, keeping the dark drip tips (grass block sides).
strip: [x0, x1] builds the tile from only those columns (shuffled), e.g. tree bark between the trunk's outlines.
recolor: hex colours, darkest to lightest, that the tile's own colours map onto by brightness (grass top: Terraria's leaf block in grass greens).
cells: frames for each mosaic cell, row by row (sunplate: Terraria's four corner pieces, so a face looks like a 2x2 patch of it).
rotate: random frame and quarter turn per mosaic cell (art with no up, seen from above); variants: how many face variants to build (default: the frame count).
outline: [left x, right x] paints those outline columns on the face's real left and right edges only.
sprite_fx: process the sprite with SpriteFx settings of that name (upscale, warp, noise; edited with ./sprite_editor.sh, saved in sprite_fx.json).
A face set to null is not drawn (sprite furniture shouldn't get a floating top face).
render: cube | cutout | cross | none. hardness: pickaxe damage multiplier, 1 / Terraria's block hit points (100 damage breaks; dirt 2.0 = 50%, ebonstone 0.5 = 200%). min_pick: required pickaxe power.
sun_through: sunlight comes straight down through it (Terraria's leaf blocks block light, not the sun).

flame: Terraria's flickering flame over a torch, candle, lamp... (TileDrawing.GetTileFlameData): its Flame_N sheet drawn count times (7) at random offsets that change every tick, x and y: [min, max, pixels per step] ([-10, 11, 0.15] and [-10, 1, 0.35]), color: brightness of each (100 of 255, added on). {} takes those defaults. ember: a torch's dust (DustID: 6 plain torch fire, 59 blue...), puffed up from it 1 in 40 ticks.
pulse: its light changes back and forth between colours a and b (Terraria's Demon Torch: DemonTorchLight, Main.demonTorch going 0 -> 1 -> 0 by step a tick); emit is its light midway.

falls: falls when nothing holds it up (Terraria's falling tiles: sand, ebonsand, crimsand, silt, slush): when the block under it goes, or it is placed over a gap, it drops as a falling block (10 damage to whatever it lands on) and settles where it lands.

near_buff: standing near one gives you that buff (Terraria's BuffID: the Bast Statue's CatBast). interact buff: right-click it for its buff (the Sharpening Station's Sharpened); interact extractinator: use an extractable item on it.
anim: an animated placeable, like Terraria's animated tiles (Main.AnimateTiles): {frames, stride: sheet pixels down to the next frame, ticks: 1/60 s each frame shows}. All of a kind animate together.

rare_drop: [item, n]: 1 time in n it drops that item instead of its drop (the sword in stone of an Enchanted Sword Shrine, Terraria's LargePiles2 style 17: the Terragrim 1 in 30, else the Enchanted Sword).

drop_chance: it drops its drop only this often (Terraria's glowing mushrooms: half the time). top_drops false: felling its tree drops no extra from the top (a giant mushroom's cap). branches false: a trunk that grows no branches (a giant mushroom's stem).
scatter: a plant sits off its cell's middle by up to this much (blocks) and turned any way, the same every time for its cell (the glowing mushrooms, so they don't stand in a grid).
rope: Terraria's ropes and chains (Main.tileRope): climbed (Player rope climbing), extended downward by placing more on them, thrown out by a Rope Coil (Ropes).

variant_of: one of that block's styles (Terraria's frames of one tile: grass, flowers, vines, rocks, pots...), each its own block so each has its own model; a new world's plants each take a random style of their kind (worldgen's scatter_styles), and everything else treats them as that block (Data.kind_of).
gem: a gem tree's trunk (Terraria's SetGemTreeDrops): each cell drops that gem 1 time in 10, else its drop (Stone Block).

Tree trunks: Terraria's plain trunk frames (GrowTree's default three twice as likely as each other set), the 16 px trunk inside each 20 px frame. Not its branch-joint frames, whose outline is open (TreeBranches' stems cover the outline instead), nor the two sets whose knots bulge past 16 px (cropped, they'd leave gaps).

cut (set from the art): its sheet is one of Terraria's Main.tileCut tiles (grass, flowers, plants, vines, cobwebs, herbs, pots...), which a swung weapon or tool and the player's projectiles break (Data.TILE_CUT, Game.cut_tile). tile_id: that sheet's Terraria tile id.

pressure_plate: "player" - stepping on it (a player, as Terraria's gray, brown and orange plates) sets off what it's wired to (worldgen's trap_wire decorations). trap: what a wire does to it - dart: shoots a Poison Dart (200 ticks between), boulder: drops the plug under it (actuated: boulder_plug) and rolls out, explosives: blows up. cracked: Terraria's cracked dungeon bricks: running or landing on them shatters them under you (Player.CheckCrackedBrickBreak), and explosions break them though the Dungeon's other bricks don't. touch_damage: touching it (standing on it too) hurts that much (Terraria's TouchDamageImmediate: Spikes 60). off / lit: a light's switched-off twin and back (a switch wired to it swaps them). interact locked_chest: its key (a Golden Key, used up; key_kept: not used up, the Shadow Key) opens it for good, turning it into unlocks_to; interact switch: right-click it to swap the light it's wired to (worldgen's 'switch' decoration), turning into toggles_to.

tool: pickaxe | axe | any (any = breaks instantly with anything). Axes do Terraria's axe power x 0.24 a hit (x axe_mult: cactus 3); pickable: a pickaxe works too. hit_to: the first pickaxe hit turns it into this (grass to dirt, like Terraria's). drop: internal Terraria item name.
